report:
The unchanged body contains a false Rossi assertion in n2. Its statement requires z∈hull(L)∖L and V relatively compact with closure disjoint from L, but does not require z∈V. That missing antecedent is essential.

Here is a counterexample with nonempty boundary hull. Take k=Q̄ with its trivial valuation, Y=A¹_k with original ring k[T], and let ξ_{a,r} denote the Gauss seminorm centered at a with radius r. Put L={ξ_{0,1}} and z=0. Every nonzero polynomial has norm 1 at ξ_{0,1}, so hull(L)={|T|≤1}; hence z∈hull(L)∖L. Choose V={|T−1|<1/2}. Its closure is the compact closed disc {|T−1|≤1/2}, disjoint from L, and its boundary is {ξ_{1,1/2}}⊂hull(L). Thus K_V={ξ_{1,1/2}}. The ORIGINAL polynomial T−1 separates z from hull(K_V): |T−1|(z)=1>1/2=sup_{K_V}|T−1|. All stated hypotheses hold, but the claimed conclusion fails.

The displayed Rossi proof needs z∈V when it asserts that the glued weight is positive at z. Adding this condition gives the neighborhood version used subsequently: the off-Z and split-piece applications explicitly choose V around their tested point. Consequently this counterexample does not itself disprove those later conditional conclusions. It does, however, prevent PASS for the complete unchanged body. Adding an essential antecedent restricts the assertion; it is not a harmless wording correction.

I audited the remaining dependencies rather than adopting the draft’s verdicts. Task background was used only within its explicit grant: task.problem, urn:xean:task, states, “The exact accepted round77 bodies and actual round80 PASS are granted background ONLY for their precise supplied partial scope and binding errata.” The canonical positive norm law, exact contact hypotheses, bridge and accepted smooth gates retain their supplied restrictions. GEO remains an antecedent at every relevant application. Neither the original equation nor singular EP is granted.

For n1, the dense principal good open can exclude both the finite map’s non-étale locus and the finite image of the original witness’s non-isomorphism locus. Monic equations control the original source generators. The good-open trace is extended on the original smooth base before any bad-fiber values are identified. Geometric integrality, the height bound and the field dimension formula apply to every minimal reduced slice component: each has dimension one and is horizontal. Normalization of the entire reduction is finite, its components are smooth over the perfect field H(s), and the total generic rank is d. The n=1 and n=0 cases have the stated interpretations.

Each normalized component lifts through the RELATIVE proper morphism P_F→Y_F, using its closed-point DVRs, spreading and separated gluing. This preserves the same witness and needs no absolute properness over F. Restricting each contact approximant before taking limits gives the harmonic-test argument; decreasing comparison closure handles the subharmonic or identically−∞ alternatives. The analytic Jacobian contraction constructs actual disc coordinates, including uniqueness over complete residue extensions. At a finite center, comparison and upper semicontinuity give the strict-disc radial limit; at a −∞ center, upper semicontinuity alone gives it.

The ramification coordinate becomes exactly t=bz^e after taking the convergent unit root in residue characteristic zero. The residual polynomial Z^e−T supplies the full completed residue degree e and uniqueness of the point above the Gauss point. Compactness of a fixed finite inverse image, with all center neighborhoods included, excludes every missing small-radius branch. Equality of polynomial norm-law coefficients on the dense good open identifies the normalized-curve specialization with the ORIGINAL residue characters. Complete-extension regrouping therefore gives the original m_y, not nonflat fiber lengths. Positive finite summation also covers a −∞ summand without compensating +∞ values. I found no additional defect in this conditional trace derivation.

For n2’s G construction, the starting membership is genuinely supplied. Including unpowered original generators makes the projective affine chart literally Spec R. The canonical potential is a_i−cg_0, with boundary C_i+cp; replacing it by a_i−cg would lose the actual reference. Compact nested-superlevel emptiness supplies the indices without discontinuous Dini convergence. The whole winning collars and the old-region/new-annulus/exterior inequalities give decreasing weights in one actual bundle. Membership precedes regularization. Same-bundle uniform approximation with summable shifts, followed by section localization and dominated generator padding, gives the stated original-ring sequence and bounds.

The denominator counterexample is correct. The replacement uses height-one valuations of the finite normalization to prove h=b^Nf^{Nc/q} integral. Finiteness of R[h] then gives ONE f^M clearing EVERY h^j into R. Hull testing these original polynomials and taking roots yields the branch error, including zero suprema. The compact decreasing-supremum argument includes sup_L v=−∞, and the successive limits yield exact principal-open hull control.

The entropy construction treats all coordinate faces. Positive finite-coordinate probabilities and p_0 give coercivity of the support difference; omitted coordinates give a separate positive gap when leaving an infinity neighborhood. Face-respecting rational grids and rational height intervals give global conjugate bounds, including the all-infinity face. The positive countable tail estimates produce decreasing upper partial sums. Rational coefficient intervals, omitted zero coefficients and decreasing floor/generator padding preserve negative logarithms and −∞ values. Support replacement is a positive construction, not subtraction of psh functions. The off-Z argument uses ORIGINAL u’s genuine local regularizability, controlled compact neighborhoods and the ordinary source-ring hull inequality. Its Rossi application does establish the missing neighborhood antecedent.

For n3, the split argument controls the entire preimage of the singleton hull and distinguishes open pieces from their compact controlled closures. It shrinks ONE neighborhood where the raw positive integer branch sum is constant, treats γ=1 separately, and retains cδ′ in the boundary gap. Every other fiber contribution lies in that same neighborhood; the displayed bounds are uniformly negative on the full boundary hull. Products and maxima retain the same witness.

Product Runge is established before the Hartogs coefficient argument. Countability supplies the controlled compact exhaustion, and the strict polynomial neighborhoods genuinely increase to the domain. The strict constant-coefficient conditions are necessary for the exact radius formula. Gauss norms at every positive real radius justify its endpoint convention; compact closed fiber discs prove convergence of radii, including infinity. Reference-winning gluing then establishes membership before original-coefficient regularization.

The descending-Z argument checks every component, not merely maximum dimension: closed-immersion images are incomparable, finiteness forces each original component to remain a component of the full inverse image, and the complementary closure omits its generic point. The localization uses exactly U=π⁻¹(S′). Jacobson coverage also applies at intermediate stages. The finite-projection argument’s extension from an integral variety to the reduced union T is supplied by its own single-fiber/cotangent/Nakayama calculation. The final U=r⁻¹(S) lies inside original Y and retains analytic injectivity after field extension. Reduced singular-stratum dimensions strictly decrease. At the final empty stratum, the argument performs the additional GLOBAL empty-Z product/Hartogs step rather than stopping with a local cover.

The limited projective consequence keeps ORIGINAL X, its sections, actual ample reference and bundles. Its chart functions have genuine cL membership before taking maxima; a maximal homogeneous coordinate recovers original φ at every point, including −∞. Varying-class closure then gives only the stated conditional countable membership consequence.

For n4, the normalization check gives constant-shift change c(V−ν(X)), so the raw target mass must be V; the dimension-zero convention is consistent. BJ12.8 uses an attained maximizer; BJ5.13 assumes approaching target EP. The envelope source explicitly calls both descent and weak/global gates. Accordingly, the retained GEO, resolved-nef fiber-value descent, singular EP, arbitrary-cardinality competitor descent and unbounded normalization/E¹ compatibility remain separate requirements. The original equation is not established. n4’s claim that all n2 assertions were proved needs qualification because of the Rossi defect above.

Two harmless clarifications are separate from that defect: generator branches in weighted sums retain their scaled positive slopes, and real additive normalizations can be implemented through decreasing rational shifts. Neither changes a limit or its antecedents. The original HAL endpoint was blocked; its supplied literal proof bodies were checked mathematically, and accessible primary research texts supplied the applied curve statements, with their stronger field/proper-curve hypotheses verified through completion and smooth projective compactification. Hashes, compilation, runtime observations and finite diagnostics played no role in the verdict.
